review_candidates.title: Lead Signaling Engineer (Wayside & Switches)
review_candidates.description_excerpt: The Candidate will be responsible for supervising signaling systems and field equipment—including point machines, track switches, and wayside signaling gear—installed by the Rail System Contractor. The scope covers installation, field testing, and troubleshooting to guarantee safe, reliable train operation. Key Responsibilities Supervise contractor installation of all wayside signaling systems and point machines. Ensure full compliance of signaling system layouts, schematics, and software config
eligibility_evidence: Thorough knowledge of international signaling standards and regulatory frameworks (e.g., AREMA, FRA, IEEE, CENELEC).
review_candidates.requirements_excerpt: Ensure full compliance of signaling system layouts, schematics, and software configurations with contractual requirements and safety regulations. Coordinate closely with civil, trackwork, and MEP engineering teams to align interface requirements. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Electronics, or Telecommunications Engineering. 5–10 years of railway engineering experience specializing in designing, installing, testing, and maintaining signaling equipment. Proficiency with CAD tools and simulation software (e.g., AutoCAD, MATLAB, signal system simulators).
